Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers here; I'm attaching a short processing diagram and our subprocessor inventory CSV for your intake team.

1) Regions / execution footprint- Hosted (Redwood API) requests are executed in the cloud region nearest to the originator by default. For US customers that generally means us-west-2 or us-east-1 (AWS) depending on latency and capacity; for EU customers we default to europe-west1 (GCP) in our EU cluster. Dedicated and Private deployments are configurable/pinned to customer-specified regions (we can run in a VPC in whichever region you choose).

2) Subprocessors that may touch inference or short-lived caches- For Hosted: primary compute runs on our managed cloud pools (we contract with AWS and GCP for region-specific capacity). We also use a GPU partner (ScaleCloud, contractual partner) for burst capacity in some regions; their involvement is limited to hosting inference containers and does not change our handling of customer data. We use Redis clusters (managed) for short-lived KV caching in region; logs are written to our telemetry pipeline then retained per your retention policy.

Cross-border transfers- For multi-region failover or routing, requests may be routed to a proximate region in a different juridiction if the primary region is constrained and your policy allows cross-border routing. If Horizon needs strict no-cross-border processing for EU-origin data, we can enable region enforcement to prevent any cross-border execution for EU traffic.

3) Deletion / retention timeline (default hosted flow)
- Request payloads: persisted for 30 days by default; can be configured to 0 days for PII-minimizing setups.
- Short-term KV/cache (model attention cache, prefix cache): ephemeral and invalidated within 1 hour of session end by default; when account-level deletion is triggered we evict caches immediately and issue a background compaction job to remove any persisted cache shards within 24 hours.
- Logs (app + telemetry): retained for 90 days by default; audit exportable on request.
- Backups/snapshots (infra-level): retained 14 days; deletion requests initiate an expedited snapshot purge process that completes within 72 hours where supported by the cloud provider.

I'm attaching: data_flow_diagram.pdf and redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv.

If you need formal evidence for procurement (SLA language / subprocessors list signed by legal), I can loop in Karthik who handles subprocessor contracts.

Regards,

Emma — quick answers:
1) KV cache replication: we do not replicate ephemeral KV cache shards across regions. For high-availability we keep active shards in the primary region and rely on our orchestration layer to rehydrate state where needed; persistent snapshots are only stored per-region unless you request cross-region backups. I can provide the architecture diagram that shows replica sets.
2) ScaleCloud: yes — they are contracted as a subprocess and we have a DPA on file. I'll pull the DPA and an attestation PDF and send to contracts (contracts@horizonhealth.com) by end of day tomorrow.

If Horizon would like region enforcement turned on for the POC, we can include that in the kickoff and place it in the SOW so routing is deterministic.
